cards.title: Protecting Routes
cards.content:
Route Guards

Route guards prevent unauthorized users from accessing certain routes or navigating away with unsaved changes. They can return a boolean, an Observable, a Promise, or a UrlTree to redirect users.

Modern Angular uses functional guards instead of classes.

cards.title: Functional Guards
cards.content:
Writing Functional Guards

A functional guard is just a function that takes route snapshots and returns true/false or a UrlTree.

export const authGuard: CanActivateFn = (route, state) => {
  const authService = inject(AuthService);
  return authService.isLoggedIn() ? true : inject(Router).createUrlTree(['/login']);
};

cards.title: Guards Summary
cards.content:
Summary

  • Guards protect routes from unauthorized access.
  • Functional guards are the modern standard, utilizing the inject() function.
  • A guard can return a UrlTree to handle redirections cleanly.
